title: Wheatear stitch
subtitle: Two straight stitches caught by a chain loop to mimic a grain head
excerpt: Wheatear stitch pairs two diagonal straight stitches to form a V, then laces a chain loop through them without entering the fabric. The result looks like a single head of wheat and can be repeated in a line or scattered as individual motifs.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), wheatear stitch entry.

content.text: Wheatear stitch has two parts. First, two straight stitches are placed so they angle toward a shared lower point, forming a V. Then the needle comes up at that lower point and is slid under both straight stitches from below, left to right, without piercing the fabric. The thread is looped under the needle tip to make a chain loop that catches and holds the V, just as in a detached chain stitch.
Bring the needle up at A on the left. Insert at B, placing B at the top of the V, slightly right of centre. This is the first diagonal straight stitch.
Bring the needle up at C on the right, mirroring A. Insert at B, entering the same hole used for the first stitch. Pull through. Two stitches now angle down to B, forming a V.
Bring the needle up at D, directly below B. Slide the needle tip from left to right under both straight stitches at the point where they meet near B, without piercing the fabric.
Loop the thread under the needle tip and pull through, forming a small chain loop at D. Insert the needle just below the loop to close it with a tiny securing stitch at E.
For a row, bring the needle up at the position that becomes the new A for the next unit, spacing units evenly down the line.

items.symptom: The chain loop is loose and floppy
items.cause: The needle is passing under the stitches too far from B, so the loop has no support.
items.fix: Pass the needle under the stitches as close to B as possible before forming the loop, so it sits snugly against the V.

items.symptom: The two straight stitches spread apart rather than forming a neat V
items.cause: A and C are placed too far from the centre or not at equal distances.
items.fix: Keep A and C equidistant from the vertical centre line and check they share the same horizontal level before stitching.

items.symptom: Units in a row are different sizes
items.cause: The spacing between D and the next A varies.
items.fix: Mark the placement points along a guide line before starting the row.
